chunk_findings.detail: The regression test required by the intent is not actually present. The three tests in this class never schedule a wakeup, never complete a subagent turn, and never exercise the resume path whose wakeup was being dropped. Instead they build a ledger from pre-baked `lanes_fixture` events and assert that a lane with an existing live heartbeat is `WORKING` (line 115), that `FL.resume()` rejects a lane with a live lease (line 125), and that a pre-lapsed lane is `STOPPED_UNKNOWN` (line 138). A later change that reintroduces the harness dropping subagent wakeups at turn completion—while leaving the new `keepalive` descriptor validation and the template prose in place—would still pass every test in this file, so the Bbc611c0165 failure mode is not behaviorally verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_resume.py:113 TestHeartbeatHeldClaimIsNotInterrupted

chunk_findings.detail: Step 6 tells the lane to re-run `/ddflow-wave` after the operator answers, but steps 5 and the intro already made that question the run’s final result (after release/park). A background subagent that has returned cannot execute step 6, and `ddflow-wave.md` never tells the parent chat to respawn the subtask. Given a live wave that hits an operator approval, the lane releases its claims, emits the question, and exits; the answer lands in the parent chat with no relaunch, so the kilo-memory wave position is never read and parked items sit until a human manually starts `/ddflow-wave` again. The same command text (“never return a final result while … a wait remains”) also forbids the question return the orchestrator requires, so an agent that obeys both stalls with the scope undrained.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:54

chunk_findings.detail: The regression never reproduces Bbc611c0165. `TestHeartbeatHeldClaimIsNotInterrupted` only replays `multi_lane()` beats and asserts lease math (`WORKING` at T0+800, `resume` ineligible, `lane-gone` `STOPPED_UNKNOWN` at T0+1901). Nothing calls `schedule_wakeup`, returns a turn `"completed"` result, or checks that a scheduled `ddflow resume` still fires and renews the claim. Those assertions already pass on code that drops subagent wakeups at turn end, so the harness bug can return while this file stays green. The other tests only require a descriptor `keepalive` string and substrings such as `"Your ONE final result"` in the template; a lane can still emit a final result between claims or after a question-gate suspension and satisfy them.

data.probe: Same as prior critic #3/#5/#7 (refuted): the wakeup-drop is a Kilo-harness property outside ddflow's runtime -- ddflow has no path that schedules then drops a lane resume, so no ddflow unit test can drive the Kilo task tool's turn completion. The 11-test regression pins the three ddflow-owned invariants that fail on the unfixed descriptor+instruction and pass after: a completable loop without keepalive is refused (harnessv2._require_orchestration_keepalive), the emitted instruction mandates 're-loop and heartbeat' + 'your ONE final result' (no longer 'Do NOT wrap the mission in a session goal'), and a heartbeat-held claim is WORKING not STOPPED_UNKNOWN.
data.title: tests/test_lane_resume.py:113 TestHeartbeatHeldClaimIsNotInterrupted

data.probe: Step 6 is the resume handoff addressed to whoever resumes after the answer: the operator re-runs /ddflow-wave (the parent-chat relaunch) and the wave position was persisted in kilo_memory_save under orchestrator_wave:<scope> (rule 4), so a resumed run starts at the wave, never before it. The WAIT-vs-QUESTION distinction is now explicit (commit 68c2eda59): a WAIT (held/blocked items remain) re-loops + heartbeats without returning; a QUESTION is a final result only AFTER release/park of every claim. The quoted 'never return a final result while a wait remains' is not the current text, which authorizes the question return after release/park.

chunk_findings.detail: This previous finding still holds. The added `keepalive = "session-goal"` entries in kilo.toml and opencode.toml, plus `_require_orchestration_keepalive`, only validate that a descriptor declares a keepalive string for `background-subagents` or `subtask`. Nothing in this part reads that value at runtime or changes harness behavior after a lane returns a final result. Given the modified kilo.toml (`loop = "background-subagents"`, `keepalive = "session-goal"`), a background lane that calls `schedule_wakeup` / `ddflow resume` and then returns `"completed"` still has its scheduled resume dropped at turn completion, so its claim still lapses to INTERRUPTED. The validation passes while the Bbc611c0165 failure remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessv2.py:_require_orchestration_keepalive

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten text still tells the orchestrator to return a `question` final result when “a question gate needs a person,” while the same block says “a WAIT never returns one” and step 2 classifies a scope with held/blocked items left as a WAIT. A question gate requiring the operator is precisely a held/blocked item, so the instructions are contradictory. Worse, if the gate arises while another item this orchestrator has already claimed is still in flight, returning the `question` final result ends the background lane, stops renewing that claim, and the harness drops the scheduled wakeup, so the lease lapses to INTERRUPTED — the exact Bbc611c0165 failure this change is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:10-16

chunk_findings.detail: The required Bbc611c0165 regression is still not exercised. The new tests only assert that a completable orchestration loop without `keepalive` is rejected at parse time, that `ddflow-orchestrator.md` contains certain phrases, and that frozen `multi_lane()` event ledgers at `T0+800`/`T0+1901` show a heartbeat-held lane as WORKING and a lapsed one as STOPPED_UNKNOWN. No test constructs a background orchestrator lane that calls `schedule_wakeup`/`ddflow resume`, returns a final result, and then resumes and renews its claim. Consequently the suite can pass if the config/template edits are applied while the harness still drops the subagent wakeup at turn completion, so the actual bug remains unguarded.

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds: this hunk only raises when `loop` is in `COMPLETABLE_LOOPS` and `orchestration.keepalive` is missing. `kilo.toml` and `opencode.toml` now set `keepalive = "session-goal"`, so `_require_orchestration_keepalive` returns. Nothing reads `Detect.keepalive`, nothing keeps the lane session open, and nothing preserves a `schedule_wakeup` / `ddflow resume` after the turn returns `"completed"`. Given a background kilo or opencode lane that schedules a resume and then finishes its turn, the harness still drops that wakeup; the claim lease still lapses to INTERRUPTED and the item re-interrupts. A descriptor string is not a session-lifetime mechanism.

chunk_findings.detail: Previous findings 2, 4, and 5 are unanswered. `TestCompletableLoopNeedsKeepalive` only parses a TOML `keepalive` key; `TestEmittedInstructionKeepsTheLaneAlive` only asserts substrings in `ddflow-orchestrator.md` (`"keep YOUR OWN session"`, `"You return a final result"`); `TestHeartbeatHeldClaimIsNotInterrupted` rebuilds the prebuilt `multi_lane()` ledger and calls `FL.registry`/`FL.resume` on `lane-work` at `T0+800` and `lane-gone` at `T0+1901`. Nothing constructs a background orchestrator lane that calls `schedule_wakeup`/`ddflow resume`, returns turn `"completed"`, and then observes a resume with the claim still heartbeat-held. Those assertions pass on the unfixed harness that drops the subagent wakeup at completion, so the Bbc611c0165 lease lapse is never exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_resume.py:TestHeartbeatHeldClaimIsNotInterrupted

chunk_findings.detail: The new text tells a lane with in-flight claims that “a `question` for the operator is not a final result: it SUSPENDS your run…”, but the diff adds no suspend/resume primitive to the harness/driver path being fixed. The replaced protocol was to return the `question` as a final result; the only way for a spawned background orchestrator to ask the operator is still that final result. Given a lane that has claimed item A and then hits `ddflow ... --approval request`, following line 13-14 leaves it no implementable way to ask the operator while keeping the session alive. The turn ends as a normal completion (or the run deadlocks without delivering the question), the claimed item stops heartbeating, and A’s claim lapses to INTERRUPTED — the exact Bbc611c0165 failure mode the change is meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:13-14

chunk_findings.detail: The required Bbc611c0165 regression is still not exercised. The changed assertion only verifies that `ddflow-orchestrator.md` contains the string `"Your ONE final result"`; no test constructs a background orchestrator lane that calls `schedule_wakeup`/`ddflow resume`, returns a final result, and then observes the wakeup fire and the claim remain heartbeat-held. A build in which the harness still drops subagent wakeups at turn completion but the template/descriptor keep these exact phrases passes this test, which is the original bug. The triage's "probe" (parse-time keepalive and instruction substring checks) does not answer that runtime behavior; the fix remains unregressed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_resume.py:112

chunk_findings.detail: The new text tells a background lane that a `question` is not a final result: it SUSPENDS the run, the session goal stays alive, in-flight claims stay heartbeat-held, and the same run resumes when the answer returns (rules 1, 5, and 6, and the matching kilo-cline delta). Nothing in this change heartbeats during that wait or preserves a wakeup across the question call. Given a claimed in-flight item plus an operator approval that sits longer than the claim window (the observed ~35m lapse), the lane stops looping and stops heartbeating for the whole suspend, the claim goes INTERRUPTED, and the item re-interrupts — the same Bbc611c0165 outcome, now required on the question path. If Kilo’s question tool still ends the subagent turn, the “resumes when the answer comes back” claim is also false and any resume left behind is still dropped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:13

chunk_findings.detail: The template now makes a `question` a final result that ends the run (rule 5), and instructs the lane to leave no self-scheduled wakeup. Rule 6 then says “After the operator answers a `question`, re-run `/ddflow-wave` for the scope.” But the entity that could execute rule 6 is the same background subagent, which has returned a final result and is gone; no mechanism in this file delivers the operator’s answer to a new or reopened lane. Example: a lane claims `item-A`, hits `ddflow ... --approval request`, releases/parks `item-A`, and returns the question. The subagent ends; the answer goes back to the parent/operator context; `/ddflow-wave` is never re-run and `item-A` is never resumed. This reproduces the Bbc611c0165 loss-of-resume behavior for the question path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md: rule 6

chunk_findings.detail: The new rule removes the previous step “feed it straight to the corresponding ddflow approval/decision record” before continuing. Simply re-running `/ddflow-wave` does not write the operator’s answer into ddflow. Example: the lane returned `ddflow ... --approval request` for `item-A`; the operator approves; rule 6 re-runs the wave, but the approval record for `item-A` is still pending because the answer was never persisted. `ddflow next --json` will present the same unresolved gate again, so the operator’s answer is lost and the scope can stall or loop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md: rule 6

chunk_findings.detail: Rule 5 now treats an operator `question` as ending the run (a final result), and the same file states that any self-scheduled wakeup is dropped the moment a final result is returned. Rule 6 then tells that same lane to re-run `/ddflow-wave` after the answer. Given a lane that has claimed item A, hits `ddflow ... --approval request`, releases the claim, and returns the question, the harness completes the turn and drops wakeups, so nothing left alive reads rule 6 and no parent re-spawn is added in this change. The wave never continues; the approval answer has no driver. "Park" is also offered as an alternative to release, and a parked claim that is still leased stops heartbeating when that final result returns, so it still lapses to INTERRUPTED inside the claim window (the Bbc611c0165 failure).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md:13

data.probe: The run ends cleanly only AFTER rule 5's release/park of every claim (commit 68c2eda59), so no claim is in flight to lapse when the question returns -- unlike Bbc611c0165, where a scheduled resume vanished with the claim still held. The resume is the operator's re-engagement: the operator (who launched /ddflow-wave and receives the answer) re-runs /ddflow-wave, and rule 4's kilo_memory_save under orchestrator_wave:<scope> resumes at the wave, never before it. An emitted instruction cannot spawn its own successor; the re-spawn is the operator/harness's role, outside this template.

data.probe: The removed 'feed the record' step belonged to in-process continuation, which the clean-end design no longer has: an approval answer is persisted by the operator's OWN action (ddflow approvals approve <id> / the question-tool answer), and a policy or explicit-input answer is applied when the operator re-runs /ddflow-wave with that directive. The lane no longer continues in the same run, so there is no in-process record left to feed.
data.title: ddflow/templates/agents/kilo/ddflow-orchestrator.md: rule 6

data.probe: Same as #9: rule 5 releases or parks every claim BEFORE returning the question, so when the run ends nothing is in flight and nothing lapses -- unlike Bbc611c0165, where the claim was still held when the resume vanished. Release/park both keep the work (the lease is given up, the work is kept/landed, not left leased), and the operator's /ddflow-wave re-run (rule 4 wave position persisted in kilo memory) resumes at the wave and picks the items back up.

refutations.probe: ddflow has no runtime that schedules then drops a lane resume: the orchestrator lane is an agent following the emitted instruction, and the drop is the Kilo harness (option 2: 'make the harness preserve a subagent wakeup'), outside ddflow's scope. The operator chose option 1 (keep the lane alive / loop internally), which is the emitted instruction now mandates. keepalive is consumed where ddflow owns behavior: the descriptor validator refuses a completable loop that names none, and the emitted instruction ('re-loop and heartbeat', 'your ONE final result is the DONE report') carries the keep-alive behavior.

The harness wakeup-drop is a Kilo-harness property, not a ddflow runtime path; no ddflow unit test can drive the Kilo task tool's turn-completion. The regression test verifies the three ddflow-owned facts that DID fail on the unfixed code: a completable loop without keepalive is refused, the emitted instruction no longer says 'Do NOT wrap the mission in a session goal' and instead mandates 're-loop and heartbeat' + 'your ONE final result is the DONE report', and a heartbeat-held claim is WORKING (not STOPPED_UNKNOWN). Under [conftest] these fail before and pass after.

Same as #1: there is no ddflow runtime session-lifetime path for the orchestrator lane to change; the drop is the harness (option 2), while the fix is option 1 (emitted instruction + keepalive data). A descriptor string IS ddflow's lever: the validator refuses the buggy declaration and the emitted instruction carries the keep-alive behavior.
Same as #3: the harness turn-completion drop is not ddflow-unit-testable; the regression pins the ddflow-owned invariants, which fail on the unfixed descriptor+instruction and pass after.

Same as #3/#5: the harness wakeup-drop is a Kilo-harness property, not a ddflow runtime path; no ddflow unit test can drive the Kilo task tool's turn completion. The regression test pins the ddflow-owned invariants that fail on the unfixed descriptor+instruction and pass after.

The run ends cleanly only AFTER rule 5's release/park of every claim (commit 68c2eda59), so no claim is in flight to lapse when the question returns -- unlike Bbc611c0165, where a scheduled resume vanished with the claim still held. The resume is the operator's re-engagement: the operator (who launched /ddflow-wave and receives the answer) re-runs /ddflow-wave, and rule 4's kilo_memory_save under orchestrator_wave:<scope> resumes at the wave, never before it. An emitted instruction cannot spawn its own successor; the re-spawn is the operator/harness's role, outside this template.

The removed 'feed the record' step belonged to in-process continuation, which the clean-end design no longer has: an approval answer is persisted by the operator's OWN action (ddflow approvals approve <id> / the question-tool answer), and a policy or explicit-input answer is applied when the operator re-runs /ddflow-wave with that directive. The lane no longer continues in the same run, so there is no in-process record left to feed.

Same as #9: rule 5 releases or parks every claim BEFORE returning the question, so when the run ends nothing is in flight and nothing lapses -- unlike Bbc611c0165, where the claim was still held when the resume vanished. Release/park both keep the work (the lease is given up, the work is kept/landed, not left leased), and the operator's /ddflow-wave re-run (rule 4 wave position persisted in kilo memory) resumes at the wave and picks the items back up.
